title: Solar PV Tracking Systems
painPoint: Utility-scale solar trackers must slew every day for 25 years, and their slew-drive motors, magnetic angle encoders, and dampers are where magnet quality decides field reliability. Vendors face three hard problems: encoder flux must stay inside a tight window so azimuth and tilt feedback remains accurate to a fraction of a degree; NdFeB output must survive irreversible loss from winter cold and 85C stowed-summer surface heat; and coatings must resist UV, sand abrasion, and coastal salt fog without blistering. Falling tracker prices squeeze magnet budgets, so batch-to-batch flux consistency and validated grades such as N42, 42SH, and 35UH matter as much as peak energy product.
youjiuSolution: For solar trackers we engineer from the duty cycle rather than the datasheet peak. Standard slew drives ship with N42 and 42SH blocks under tight flux screening, desert and hot-climate projects move to 35UH so coercivity holds above 85C surface temperature, and cold-climate azimuth encoders use 42SH sintered rings ground to plus or minus 0.03 mm for repeatable angle output. Outdoor parts receive NiCuNi plus epoxy or zinc-aluminum coating, verified by 720-hour neutral salt spray and 1000-hour UV exposure. Send your tracker torque profile, annual cycle count, and ambient temperature range, and our engineers will return a grade, coating, and tolerance proposal with quotation.
